questions.q: On which day does Genesis 1 create the birds?
questions.explain: Birds are made on Day 5 with the sea creatures (1:20–23). Day 6 is land animals and humans.

questions.q: Which is the real Hebrew wordplay in Genesis 2:23?
questions.explain: The pun is ish / ishah. ‘Wow-man’ works only in English. The two Hebrew words are probably not related, so the pun works by sound.

questions.q: What is wrong with the argument ‘the Hebrew word for male is connected to ‘remember’, so men are to remember what God said’?
options: Nothing, it is a standard reading
Word meaning comes from use in context, not from shared letters (the ‘root fallacy’)
questions.explain: Even if the two words were related, meaning is set by use. Nothing in Genesis 3 says that the man’s task was memory.

questions.q: What does ezer (‘helper’) in Genesis 2:18 tell us?
options: The word is often used of God as Israel’s help, so it does not imply a lower rank
questions.explain: Ezer means ‘help’. It is used of God (Psalm 121:2; Deuteronomy 33:26), so it carries no inferiority. ‘Life-saver’ is a gloss and not a translation.

questions.q: Who first adds ‘neither shall you touch it’ about the tree?
options: The text does not say; Eve reports it in 3:3, and ancient readers blame Eve or Adam
questions.explain: God’s words in 2:16–17 have no ‘touch’. Genesis Rabbah blames Eve, while Avot de-Rabbi Natan and Rashi say that Adam added a ‘fence’.

questions.q: Which statement about Genesis 3:6 is supported by the text?
questions.explain: The Hebrew has ‘with her’ (immah). Whether it means he was at the scene is argued, but ‘headship’ and ‘leading’ do not appear and God questions both.

questions.q: What does Genesis 3:21 say?
options: God killed animals as a sacrifice for sin
God made garments of skin and clothed them
questions.explain: The verse names no altar, blood or sacrifice. Christian readers see a pointer to atonement, but that is reception, not the text.

questions.q: Who gives the earliest clear Christian reading of Genesis 3:15 as being about Christ in surviving texts?
questions.explain: Irenaeus (c. 180, Against Heresies 3.23.7 and 5.21.1). Luther made ‘first gospel’ the standard label. Targums read the verse differently, and scholars still argue about earlier Jewish views.

questions.q: What does the pun in Genesis 4:1 connect Cain’s name to?
questions.explain: Eve says qanithi (‘I have acquired’). Many scholars also think the name itself means ‘smith’. ‘Treasure’ has no support.

questions.q: In Genesis 4:13–14, Cain…
options: protests that the consequence is too much, and fears for his life
questions.explain: No confession is recorded. The key word avon can mean ‘guilt’ or ‘punishment’, but Cain asks for nothing and God protects him anyway.

questions.q: What is different about the descriptions of the two offerings in Genesis 4:3–4?
options: Only Abel’s offering is called ‘firstborn’ and ‘fat portions’
Only Cain’s was on an altar
questions.explain: Only Abel’s has these words. The text gives no reason, but Hebrews 11:4 says ‘by faith’.

questions.q: Which statement about Lamech’s poem (4:23–24) is safest?
options: He whispers it out of fear
It is a boast about vengeance, and the first words can mean ‘I have killed’ or ‘I would kill’
questions.explain: The poem is a boast (the ‘Song of the Sword’). The grammar of the first clause is debated, and the text never says whom he killed.

questions.q: Which is a visible difference between Genesis 1 and Genesis 2?
options: In chapter 1 humans are made last; in chapter 2 the man is made before the animals
Only chapter 2 has a serpent and chapter 1 has none, so they are by different authors
questions.explain: The order differs, and so do the divine names (Elohim; YHWH Elohim). Scholars explain this as two sources or as a deliberate ‘zoom-in’, but the difference itself is not in dispute.

questions.q: What fruit does Genesis 3 name?
questions.explain: Genesis never names the species. The apple is a later European picture, and the popular Latin-pun story about its origin is itself disputed.

questions.q: In Genesis 3, who or what does God call ‘cursed’?
questions.explain: The serpent (3:14) and the ground (3:17). The man and woman receive consequences. Cain is later called cursed (4:11).

questions.q: What does Genesis say the sign on Cain was?
options: It does not say; its purpose was to protect him
questions.explain: The text gives no description. Its purpose is protection. The racial reading was added centuries later and has no basis in the verse.

questions.q: When does the man first get work to do?
options: Before the fall (2:15): to work and keep the garden
questions.explain: Work comes first, in 2:15. The fall makes it toil, with the ground cursed, but work itself is not the punishment.

questions.q: How many Hebrew words does Genesis 1:1 have?
questions.explain: Seven (and 1:2 has fourteen). Whether the count was planned is an inference, but the number seven shapes the whole passage.

questions.q: How does Genesis 1 refer to the sun and the moon?
options: As ‘the greater light’ and ‘the lesser light’
questions.explain: Neither is named. In neighbouring cultures they were gods. Many readers see a quiet statement that they are only lamps.

questions.q: What does the Hebrew word play on ‘naked’ (2:25) and ‘crafty’ (3:1) rest on?
options: Both come from the same word, arum / arummim, with two senses
questions.explain: The two words sound alike (arummim and arum). The man and woman are exposed, and the serpent is clever.

questions.q: In what order does God investigate in Genesis 3?
options: Man, then woman; the serpent is not asked
questions.explain: God asks the man (3:9) then the woman (3:13). The serpent is not questioned. The sentences then run serpent, woman, man.

questions.q: Which verse shares the words ‘desire’ (teshuqah) and ‘rule’ (mashal) with Genesis 3:16?
questions.explain: God tells Cain that sin’s ‘desire is for you, but you must rule over it’. What the echo means for 3:16 is debated, and both verses describe, they do not command.

questions.q: What does Lamech in Seth’s line (Genesis 5:29) do?
options: Names his son Noah in hope of relief from work
questions.explain: The Lamech of Cain’s line boasts of vengeance. The Lamech of Seth’s line names Noah (‘relief’) in hope.

questions.q: Which pair of verbs in Genesis 2:15 also describes the Levites’ work at the tent of meeting?
questions.explain: ‘To work it and keep it’ (la‘avdah ulshomrah) uses the same pair as Numbers 3:7–8 and 8:26. Scholars read this as a hint that Eden is a sanctuary. It is a proposal, not a settled fact.
